# Canonical test corpus

A minimal, self-generated corpus of DWG files that CI runs
`coverage_report` against (task #94). Four files, one per DWG version
the write path can assemble, ~1.2 KB each.

| File                  | Version        | Entities | decoded / skip / err | ratio |
|-----------------------|----------------|----------|----------------------|-------|
| `synthetic_2004.dwg`  | AC1018 (R2004) | 5        | 5 / 0 / 0            | 100 % |
| `synthetic_2010.dwg`  | AC1024 (R2010) | 5        | 5 / 0 / 0            | 100 % |
| `synthetic_2013.dwg`  | AC1027 (R2013) | 5        | 5 / 0 / 0            | 100 % |
| `synthetic_2018.dwg`  | AC1032 (R2018) | 5        | 5 / 0 / 0            | 100 % |
| **TOTAL**             |                | 20       | 20 / 0 / 0           | 100 % |

Each file carries three sections — `AcDb:Header` (64 zero bytes,
placeholder), `AcDb:Handles`, `AcDb:AcDbObjects` — and five entities:
a 2D LINE, a 3D LINE with non-default thickness and extrusion, a
CIRCLE, an ARC, and a POINT.

## Licence and provenance

**Apache-2.0, same as the rest of this repository.** These files are
generated byte-for-byte by code in this repository; not one byte
originates from an Autodesk-, Open-Design-Alliance-, or other
third-party-produced DWG. Nothing here is vendored, and no external
corpus is redistributed. This is why the corpus can be committed at
all — the obvious external candidate (`nextgis/dwg_samples`) declares
no licence, so its contents are not redistributable.

Generator: [`examples/build_fixtures.rs`](../../../examples/build_fixtures.rs),
driving `dwg::file_writer::assemble_dwg_bytes` (write-path Stages 1-5),
`dwg::handle_map::write_handle_map`, and the
`dwg::element_encoder::ElementEncoder` entity encoders.

Command line:

```sh
cargo run --release --example build_fixtures
```

First generated on top of `main` at commit `075f3fe`
("deps(deps): bump the patch-updates group across 1 directory with 4
updates (#11)"), with `examples/build_fixtures.rs` added in the same
change that committed these files.

Generation is byte-deterministic: re-running the command on an
unchanged tree leaves `git status` clean. If a future change to the
writer, the LZ77 encoder, the handle-map writer, or the entity
encoders legitimately alters the output, regenerate and commit the new
bytes in the same PR — the diff is the evidence that the change was
intentional.

## Honest scope

These fixtures prove **our reader round-trips our writer**. They are
not evidence that AutoCAD, BricsCAD, or LibreCAD accept the bytes; see
the acceptance statement in `src/file_writer.rs`. CI does not run any
Autodesk product.

Coverage is limited to the four entity types that currently have an
`ElementEncoder` implementation (LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, POINT). Add
fixtures as more encoders land — every new encoder is a chance to widen
this gate. `assemble_dwg_bytes` rejects R14 / R2000 (flat locator
table) and R2007 (two-layer Sec_Mask), so no fixture exists for those
versions yet.

## What CI does with this

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job **Coverage smoke test (canonical
corpus)**:

- fails outright if this directory holds no `.dwg` file (the job used
  to skip with a warning, which made it a vacuous gate),
- runs `cargo run --release --example coverage_report -- tests/fixtures/canonical`,
- parses the aggregate `ratio%` off the `TOTAL` row and fails below the
  threshold stated in the workflow.

The tight companion gate is [`tests/canonical_corpus.rs`](../../canonical_corpus.rs),
which runs under `cargo test` and pins the exact per-file entity counts
*and* decoded field values — so a bit-alignment regression that still
"decodes" into garbage coordinates fails there even when the ratio
would stay at 100 %.

A regression that breaks the entity walker, the common-entity preamble,
LINE / CIRCLE / ARC / POINT decoding, the section map, or the handle
map trips one or both guards.
